column3: According to Sedgewick and Wayne, the interval intersection problem gives n closed intervals [ai, bi] and asks for all pairs of intervals that overlap.
Their sweep line considers events in ascending order of endpoints, where an event is either a left endpoint or a right endpoint, and maintains a symbol table of active intervals.
According to Sedgewick and Wayne, when the sweep line considers the left endpoint of interval i, every interval in the symbol table is an intersection with interval i.
When it considers the right endpoint of interval i, it removes interval i from the symbol table.
They also pose the overlapping intervals problem: given N intervals (a_i, b_i) on the x-axis, find a point x that is contained in the maximum number of intervals.
